## Understanding Supercomputing and Researcher Demand

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
What is Supercomputing (HPC)?
</div>

High-performance computing (HPC) uses **many processors working together** to solve complex problems, run simulations, and analyse large datasets at a scale that ordinary computers cannot easily achieve.

**What makes it different?** Supercomputers combine thousands of CPU cores, often supported by GPUs, to perform calculations **in parallel**.

**Research applications:** Climate modelling, weather forecasting, drug discovery, and engineering simulations.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Understanding Researcher Demand
</div>

- [**Demand (Requested)**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Computing resources researchers **request** for their research.
- [**Allocated**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Computing resources facilities **provide** to researchers.
- [**Unmet demand**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: The portion of requests **not fulfilled**, when the measures are comparable.

::: {style="margin-top: 10px; padding: 8px 14px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB; font-size: 0.85em;"}

**Important:** Historical demand is not always directly observed. Some values are estimated using allocations or proxies, so the forecasts represent **planning scenarios rather than exact predictions**.

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.45em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Sources: IBM, *What Is High-Performance Computing?*; NCI, *NCMAS 2026 Outcomes*. Demand definitions and limitations: this project's data harmonisation methodology.

:::

## Research Objective and Scope

::: {style="margin-top: 35px;"}

**Research question**

How might demand for Australia's national research supercomputing infrastructure **change through 2030**?

<div style="height: 25px;"></div>

**Project objectives**

1. [**Collect and integrate**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} historical data from NCI and Pawsey.
2. [**Standardise and harmonise**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} resource units, reporting periods, and research classifications.
3. [**Develop and evaluate**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} transparent forecasting models.
4. [**Forecast demand**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} for overall HPC, CPU, and GPU resources through 2030.
5. [**Explore scenarios**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} for different Fields of Research (FoR).

<div style="height: 25px;"></div>

**Planning purpose**

Provide **evidence-informed scenarios** to support decisions about Australia's future national research computing infrastructure.

:::


## How Is Supercomputing Demand Measured?

::: {style="margin-top: 35px;"}

**Three Key Measurements**

- [**CPU core-hours**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Number of CPU cores used × hours of use.
- [**GPU-hours**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Number of GPUs used × hours of use.
- [**Service units (SU)**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Accounting units used by HPC facilities to measure computing resource usage.

<div style="height: 30px;"></div>

**Simple Examples**

- **CPU:** 100 CPU cores × 10 hours = **1,000 CPU core-hours**.
- **GPU:** 4 GPUs × 10 hours = **40 GPU-hours**.
- **Overall HPC:** Expressed in **kSU (thousands of service units)** in this project.

<div style="height: 30px;"></div>

::: {style="padding: 12px 18px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB;"}

**Important:** CPU core-hours, GPU-hours, and service units are **not directly interchangeable**. Service-unit conversion rules can differ across HPC systems.

:::

:::


## Data Sources and Historical Coverage

::: {style="margin-top: 35px;"}

**Primary Data Sources**

- [**NCI**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} : National Computational Infrastructure.
- [**Pawsey**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} : Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre.
- [**NCMAS**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} : National Computational Merit Allocation Scheme.

<div style="height: 25px;"></div>

**Historical Coverage: 2014 - 2026**

- **Overall HPC:** 2014 - 2026, measured in thousands of service units (kSU).
- **CPU:** 2014 - 2026, measured in million CPU core-hours.
- **GPU:** 2022 - 2026, measured in million GPU-hours.
- **Fields of Research (FoR):** Historical allocation shares by research discipline.

<div style="height: 25px;"></div>

::: {style="padding: 12px 18px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB;"}

**Data limitation:** Historical records combine reported values, derived estimates, and proxies. Coverage and measurement methods differ across years and facilities.

:::

<div style="height: 15px;"></div>

::: {style="font-size: 0.60em; color: #666;"}

Sources: NCI and Pawsey annual reports; NCMAS allocation outcomes. See project bibliography.

:::

:::

<div class="prov-panel">

<strong>What does this mean?</strong>

<ul>
<li>Allocation is mostly directly reported.</li>
<li>Demand combines direct observations, derived values, and proxies.</li>
<li>Not every year measures the same underlying quantity.</li>
</ul>

</div>

<div class="prov-panel" style="margin-top: 14px; background: #FFF5EB;">

<strong>Main limitations</strong>

<ul>
<li>Different units and accounting rules.</li>
<li>Changes in reporting scope.</li>
<li>Historical conversion assumptions.</li>
<li>Incomplete CPU/GPU separation.</li>
</ul>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="prov-takeaway">
<strong>Key takeaway:</strong> Historical demand contains more estimated values than allocation. Forecasts are therefore planning scenarios, not exact measures of total researcher need.
</div>


## Historical Computing Demand by Resource Type


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| out-width: 100%

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Load the same historical dataset used in Chapter 06
annual_converted <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/annual_demand_allocation_converted.rds"
)

# Prepare demand and allocation for all three resource types
historical_plot <- annual_converted |>
  transmute(
    year = as.integer(year),

    # Overall HPC: million kSU
    `Overall HPC|Demand` = demand_ksu / 1e6,
    `Overall HPC|Allocation` = allocation_ksu / 1e6,

    # CPU: million CPU core-hours
    `CPU|Demand` = demand_cpu_core_hours / 1e6,
    `CPU|Allocation` = allocation_cpu_core_hours / 1e6,

    # GPU: million GPU-hours (2022 onwards)
    `GPU|Demand` = if_else(
      year >= 2022,
      demand_gpu_hours / 1e6,
      NA_real_
    ),
    `GPU|Allocation` = if_else(
      year >= 2022,
      allocation_gpu_hours / 1e6,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -year,
    names_to = c("resource", "measure"),
    names_sep = "\\|",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(
    resource = factor(
      resource,
      levels = c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
      labels = c(
        "Overall HPC (million kSU)",
        "CPU (million core-hours)",
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)"
      )
    ),
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("Demand", "Allocation")
    )
  )

# Three-panel historical chart
ggplot(
  historical_plot,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = value,
    colour = measure,
    group = measure
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.25) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~resource,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Demand" = "#006DAE",
      "Allocation" = "#E69F00"
    ),
    breaks = c("Demand", "Allocation")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = function(x) {
      if (min(x) >= 2022) {
        seq(2022, 2026, by = 1)
      } else {
        c(2014, 2017, 2020, 2023, 2026)
      }
    }
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL,
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 15,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "#17324D"
    ),
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#EAF2F9",
      colour = NA
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 11
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 5, 10)
  )
```


::: {style="display: flex; gap: 15px; margin-top: 15px;"}

::: {style="flex: 1; padding: 14px; background: #F2F7FB; border-top: 4px solid #006DAE;"}

**Overall HPC**

**+43.3%** requested in 2026.

Allocation remained near **0.87 million kSU**.

:::

::: {style="flex: 1; padding: 14px; background: #F2F7FB; border-top: 4px solid #006DAE;"}

**CPU**

Historical coverage spans **2014 - 2026**.

A longer series supports trend-based model evaluation.

:::

::: {style="flex: 1; padding: 14px; background: #F2F7FB; border-top: 4px solid #006DAE;"}

**GPU**

Only **five annual observations** (2022 - 2026).

Long-term projections are particularly uncertain.

:::
